issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate (task name and solution implementation), but the template defines a function named create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate instead. This name mismatch means students following the problem text will look for create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate in the template and not find it (or will be unsure which function to implement), creating confusion and a small barrier to getting started.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template use the same function name as in the problem statement and solution. Rename template_repository/tensor_networks.py:create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate to create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate (keeping its signature and behavior), or add a small wrapper create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate that calls create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate. Also update any header comments to consistently refer to a single name.

issues.description: The tensor-networks two-qubit-gate factory is named inconsistently: the problem statement and the solution expect/create a function called create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate, but the template stub defines create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate. This mismatch makes it unclear which function students should implement and will lead to confusion (and failing tests) when students follow the problem text but edit the template with the different name.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the template stub to match the problem statement and solution: change the function create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate(...) in template_repository/tensor_networks.py to create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate(...). Also update any internal references and the docstring in the template to use the same identifier so students can directly map the requirement to the stub.
